title: Move over Sondheim, this guy knows what’s up! #broadway #musicaltheat...
transcript: The funniest interaction I've ever had with a fellow audience member at a Broadway show was in, I don't know, maybe 2016. I was seeing Bright Star on Broadway. You guys remember Bright Star? Understandable if not. It was like a bluegrass musical co-written by Steve Martin, and Carmen Cusack was the lead. And importantly, the first act ends with someone throwing a baby off a train in a duffel bag, which was a kind of widely regarded as a ridiculous moment, partly just in the concept, but also in the execution, because they did it as kind of this, like, slow mo spotlight on the duffel bag kind of twirling in the air. But anyway, I was down in the bathroom line at intermission, and there was a guy in front of me who was like a middle aged guy and I think kind of drunk. Like, his face was all red. And I did not say a single word to this man Completely unprompted, he turns around to me, looks me dead in the eye, and very, very seriously says, if you ever write a musical, do not end the first act with someone throwing a baby off a train. Because now it's already been done. And I think about that constantly. And I've never written a musical, but you could be damn sure if I ever do, I'm taking his advice.
classificationReason: Anecdote about seeing Bright Star on Broadway in 2016 and a funny interaction with another audience member. Bright Star is not on the list, and the clip contains no review of a current production.
